text:
mike: forwarding an escalated ticket from a customer. they say rerank results are nonsense when they pass their own embeddings. example payloads below — they say the reranker accepted the request but scores look arbitrary. billing/latency also spiked. can someone triage? :eyes:

ashley: thanks. do we have the raw payloads + which embed/rerank models they used?

mike: pasted from customer (redacted):

```json
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  \"model\": \"redwood-embed-large-v2\",
  \"input\": [\"Product description...\"]
}

-- returns vectors of length 1536
```

and then they call rerank like this:

```json
POST /v1/rerank
{
  \"model\": \"rerank-compact-768\",
  \"query_embedding\": [0.123, 0.456, ...],  // vector length 1536 from above
  \"candidates\": [
    {\"id\": 1, \"text\": \"Candidate A\"},
    {\"id\": 2, \"text\": \"Candidate B\"}
  ]
}

-- API returns HTTP 200 and a scores array, but ranks are wrong (A > B even tho similarity should be opposite).
```

jordan: that screams embedding-dimension mismatch. rerank-compact-768 expects 768-d vectors. if you pass a 1536-d vector the server should reject, but looks like we let it through and then do a fallback/scoring path that produces garbage.

sarah: quick sanity check: customer should be able to do len(vec) on their side. ask them to dump len(query_embedding) and len(candidate_embedding[0]). also ask for the exact model names the embed call returned (sometimes variant suffixes differ).

mike: customer replied: both query and candidate embeddings are 1536. they used \"redwood-embed-large-v2\" for both, then hit rerank-compact-768. they expected rerank to accept arbitrary dims or internally project, but it just returned odd scores. attached sample scores: [0.02, 0.97] where similarity matrix indicates reverse.

ashley: do we have any logs showing we attempted an internal projection? we should either project consistently or fail with 4xx. silent acceptance is dangerous (and billable).

jordan: agreed. minimal repro for us to run locally: curl examples below. also a tiny python checker: 

```python
# verify embedding length
def check(vec, expected=768):
    if len(vec) != expected:
        raise ValueError(f\"embedding length mismatch: got {len(vec)}, expected {expected}\")

# hacky padding/truncation if customer insists on in-band fix
def coerce(vec, expected=768):
    if len(vec) > expected:
        return vec[:expected]
    return vec + [0.0] * (expected - len(vec))
```

sarah: note: coercing dimensions is a risky hack. it changes geometry. preferred fixes: 1) re-embed with the model that matches rerank (redwood-embed-compact-768) OR 2) call rerank with raw candidate text instead of embeddings (if API supports it) OR 3) run an explicit projection using a trained matrix (not safe to do on server transparently).

mike: customer asked why they were billed for both calls if results were invalid. they want a partial refund if we made a server-side change. can we check if our service performed any extra compute (fallback scoring) after accepting mismatched dims?

ashley: i'll pull logs for that timespan. @sre-oncall can you also check if we did any fallback path (cosine fallback or text fallback) and how much compute it consumed?

sre-oncall: taking this. i see rerank accepted the request at 2026-03-12T14:02:11Z and routed to rerank-v2. our runtime attempted a distance computation: it called a generic dot-prod path which treats vectors as length-N arrays. because the implementation used no strict dimension guard, it did pairwise multiply up to min(lenA,lenB). that produced inconsistent scores. compute was modest (2ms per pair) but we definitely charged for both calls. i'll add an instrumentation spike to flag dimension mismatches.

jordan: thanks. sounds like two fixes: short-term: reject requests where embedding length != expected with HTTP 400 and an error code like \"embedding_dimension_mismatch\". long-term: add clear docs and SDK client-side guard and a server-side metric/exposure.

mike: can we push a quick patch? customer is blocking on this for production.

sre-oncall: we can ship a hotfix that validates dimensions and returns 400. i'll open a PR for runtime guard and a changelog entry. low-risk.

rerank-bot: automated note: created internal issue RNK-5482 for \"reject embedding dimension mismatches\" and assigned to eng-runtime.

ashley: also adding a recommended support response template so CS can reply: 

"Thanks — we found a dimension mismatch between your embedding model and the rerank model. As a quick fix, re-run embeddings using \"redwood-embed-compact-768\" (or call rerank with raw candidate text). We're rolling out a server-side guard to reject mismatched dims to prevent silent failures. Apologies for the confusion; we'll review billing for these requests if our change caused incorrect results." :+1:

mike: thanks all. i'll send the customer the template and let them know we're patching. filing internal followups: RNK-5482 (runtime guard), BILL-1120 (billing review if charges applied incorrectly).

sarah: one more proactive idea: add an SDK helper that raises on mismatch and can optionally auto-convert by PCA projection trained on a small sample. we should put that in devex backlog.

jordan: agree — add to backlog after hotfix.

mike: marking this resolved for now once hotfix merges. will follow up with customer. :white_check_mark:
